critical_code_review_comments: server.py:434-437 — compute_budget_alerts defines an unused MongoDB pipeline variable, then does a full collection scan of transactions and filters in Python by 'date startswith YYYY-MM'. This is O(n) per POST /transactions when a budget exists. For scale, use a proper $match on owner_id + type + category with a stringified date-prefix or a real Date field. Not blocking now (limit 5000).

get_current_user runs ensure_personal_ledger + a second users.find_one on every authenticated request. The backfill loop over 5 collections runs even when it's a no-op (personal_ledger_id already set) — actually it's guarded by `if not personal_id`, so it's only expensive once per user. OK.

Ledger 'invite_code' uniqueness is not enforced at DB level (only an index on invite_code but not unique). Extremely low collision risk with 30^6=~729M keys but consider adding unique index for robustness.

Budget breach frontend uses navigator.serviceWorker for showBudgetNotification but toast fallback works and is user-facing — the 'browser Notification API best-effort' behaviour is acceptable per spec.

AddTransactionDialog handles the new response shape via `data?.budget_alerts?.length > 0` — safely optional, but old callers of POST /transactions in tests will now break unless updated (fixed iteration2.py as courtesy).
Files under 700 LOC OK. server.py is 1050 lines — approaching limit; consider splitting into routers per resource next iteration.

context_for_next_testing_agent: test_iteration5.py MUST be run serially (not with pytest-xdist -n). Reason: the demo user is shared across xdist workers, so parallel tests that switch the demo user's current_ledger_id race with each other and cause spurious data-isolation failures. pytest.ini has -n auto; use `-o addopts=''` to disable. Verified 49/49 pass serially. All v3 features (dark mode, exports, ledgers, budget alerts) are wired correctly end-to-end. No open bugs.
